If the patch has spread in the walls of the house, the priest is to order the stones with the patch on them pulled out and thrown into an unclean place outside the town. He is to have the inside of the house scraped all around, and the plaster that is scraped off is to be dumped in an unclean place outside the town. Then they are to take other stones and put them in place of the old ones, and new plaster is to be used to replaster the house. If the patch comes back and breaks out again in the house after the stones have been pulled out and the house scraped and replastered, the priest is to come and look. If the patch has spread in the house, it is a spreading mold in the house. The house is unclean. The house must be torn down, its stones, its timbers and all its plaster, and everything carried out of the town to an unclean place. Anyone who goes into the house while it is shut up will be unclean until evening. Anyone who sleeps in the house must wash their clothes, and anyone who eats in the house must wash their clothes. But if the priest comes and looks and the patch has not spread in the house after it was replastered, he is to declare the house clean, because the mold is gone. To purify the house he is to take two birds, with some cedar wood, scarlet yarn and hyssop. He is to slaughter one of the birds over fresh water held in a clay pot. Then he is to take the cedar wood, the hyssop, the scarlet yarn and the live bird, dip them in the blood of the dead bird and in the fresh water, and sprinkle the house seven times. So he will purify the house with the bird’s blood, the fresh water, the live bird, the cedar wood, the hyssop and the scarlet yarn. He is to set the live bird free outside the town in the open country. So he will make atonement for the house, and it will be clean. This is the law for every kind of serious skin disease, for a scaly itch, for mold in clothing and in a house, and for a swelling, a scab or a bright spot, for teaching which day a thing is unclean and which day it is clean. This is the law for serious skin disease and mold.”

fields.title: Leviticus 15
fields.body_html:
A man’s discharge

The LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron. He said, “Speak to the Israelites and tell them: ‘When any man has a discharge from his body, the discharge makes him unclean. This is the uncleanness his discharge brings: whether his body lets the discharge flow or it is stopped up, either way he is unclean. Any bed that the man with the discharge lies on becomes unclean, and so does any object he sits on. Whoever touches his bed is to wash their clothes and bathe in water, and they remain unclean until evening. Whoever sits on anything the man with the discharge has sat on is to wash their clothes and bathe in water, and they remain unclean until evening. Whoever touches the body of the man with the discharge is to wash their clothes and bathe in water, and they remain unclean until evening. When the man with the discharge spits on someone who is clean, that person is to wash their clothes and bathe in water, and they remain unclean until evening. Any saddle the man with the discharge rides on becomes unclean. Anyone who touches anything that was under him will be unclean until evening, and whoever carries such things is to wash their clothes and bathe in water, and they remain unclean until evening. If the man with the discharge touches someone without first rinsing his hands in water, that person is to wash their clothes and bathe in water, and they remain unclean until evening. If the man with the discharge touches a clay pot, it is to be broken; if he touches a wooden container, it is to be rinsed in water. When the man with the discharge is healed of it, he is to count seven days for his cleansing. Then he is to wash his clothes and bathe his body in fresh water, and he will be clean. On the eighth day he is to get two turtledoves or two young pigeons and bring them before the LORD to the entrance of the tent of meeting, where he gives them to the priest. The priest is to offer one bird as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering, and so make atonement for him before the LORD on account of his discharge.

A man’s emission of semen

If semen comes out of a man, he is to bathe his whole body in water, and he remains unclean until evening. If semen gets on any piece of clothing or leather, it is to be washed in water and will stay unclean until evening.

Sexual relations and a woman’s period

When a man lies with a woman and semen is released, both of them are to bathe in water, and they remain unclean until evening. When a woman has a discharge, and what flows from her body is blood, her monthly period keeps her unclean for seven days. Anyone who touches her will be unclean until evening. During her period, whatever she lies on and whatever she sits on becomes unclean. Whoever touches her bed is to wash their clothes and bathe in water, and they remain unclean until evening. Whoever touches any object she has sat on is to wash their clothes and bathe in water, and they remain unclean until evening. Even if something is lying on her bed or on the seat she uses, whoever touches it will be unclean until evening. If a man actually lies with her and the impurity of her period gets on him, he will be unclean seven days. Every bed he lies on will also become unclean.

A woman’s prolonged flow of blood

A woman may have a flow of blood for many days when it is not the time of her period, or a flow that goes on past her period. All the days of that unclean flow she is to be as she is in the days of her period: she is unclean. All the time the flow lasts, any bed she lies on is to be treated like her bed during her period, and any object she sits on becomes unclean, as it would during her period. Whoever touches these things becomes unclean. They are to wash their clothes and bathe in water, and they remain unclean until evening. Once her flow has stopped, she is to count seven days; then she will be clean. On the eighth day she is to get two turtledoves or two young pigeons and bring them to the priest at the entrance of the tent of meeting. The priest is to offer one bird as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering, and so make atonement for her before the LORD on account of her unclean flow.’ You must keep the Israelites apart from their uncleanness, so that it does not bring death on them when they defile my tabernacle, which is among them. These are the instructions for the man with a discharge, for a man whose semen comes out from him and makes him unclean, for the woman who is unwell with her monthly period, for anyone, male or female, who has a discharge, and for the man who lies with a woman while she is unclean.”

fields.title: Leviticus 16
fields.body_html:
The Day of Atonement

The LORD spoke to Moses after Aaron’s two sons had come near to the LORD and died. The LORD said to Moses, “Speak to your brother Aaron. He may not go at any time he pleases into the Most Holy Place behind the curtain, before the mercy seat that is on the ark, so that he will not die. For it is in the cloud above the mercy seat that I appear. Aaron may enter the Most Holy Place only in this way: with a young bull for a sin offering and a ram for a burnt offering. He must be dressed in the holy linen tunic, with linen undergarments on his body, a linen sash tied around him and a linen turban wound on his head. Because these garments are holy, he is to wash his body in water and then put them on. From the congregation of the Israelites he is to take two male goats for a sin offering and one ram for a burnt offering. Aaron is to bring forward the bull that is the sin offering for himself, and so make atonement for himself and those of his household. He is to take the two goats and have them stand before the LORD at the entrance of the tent of meeting. Over the two goats Aaron is to cast two lots, one lot for the LORD and one lot for Azazel. Aaron is then to bring forward the goat picked by the lot for the LORD and offer it as a sin offering. The goat picked by the lot for Azazel, however, is to be set alive before the LORD, so that atonement may be made with it by sending it off into the wilderness to Azazel. Aaron is to bring forward the bull of his own sin offering and make atonement for himself and his household. He is to slaughter this bull. He is to fill a censer with burning coals from the altar that stands before the LORD, take two handfuls of fragrant incense ground fine, and carry them in behind the curtain. There before the LORD he is to lay the incense on the fire, and the cloud of incense will cover the mercy seat above the testimony. So he will not die. Some of the bull’s blood he is to take and sprinkle with his finger on the east side of the mercy seat, on its front. In front of the mercy seat, too, he is to sprinkle some of the blood with his finger, seven times. Then he is to slaughter the goat that is the sin offering for the people and bring its blood inside the curtain. He is to do with this blood what he did with the bull’s blood, sprinkling it on the mercy seat and before it. So he will make atonement for the Most Holy Place, cleansing it from the impurities of the Israelites, from their rebellious acts and all their sins. He is to do the same for the tent of meeting, which stays with them right among their impurities. While Aaron is inside making atonement in the Most Holy Place, no one may be in the tent of meeting until he comes out again. He makes atonement for himself, for his household and for the whole assembly of Israel. Next he is to go out to the altar before the LORD and make atonement for it. Taking some of the blood of the bull and of the goat, he is to put it on the horns of the altar on every side. He is to sprinkle some of the blood on the altar with his finger seven times. So he will purify it from the impurities of the Israelites and make it holy again. Once he has completed the atonement for the Most Holy Place, the tent of meeting and the altar, he is to present the goat that is still alive. Aaron is to lay both his hands on the live goat’s head and confess over it all the wrongdoing of the Israelites, all their rebellious acts, all their sins. So he is to place them on the goat’s head, and send it off into the wilderness with a man kept ready for that purpose. The goat will carry all their wrongdoing on itself into a barren land, and the man is to set the goat free in the wilderness. After that Aaron is to go into the tent of meeting. There he is to take off the linen garments he put on to enter the Most Holy Place, and leave them in the tent. He is to wash his body with water in a holy place and dress in his usual garments. Then he is to come out and offer the burnt offering for himself and the one for the people, making atonement for himself and the people. The fat of the sin offering he is to burn on the altar. The man who led the goat away to Azazel is to wash his clothes and bathe in water before he comes back into the camp. As for the bull and the goat of the sin offerings, whose blood was taken into the Most Holy Place for atonement, someone is to carry them outside the camp, and there their skins, meat and dung are to be burned. The one who burns them is to wash his clothes and bathe in water before he comes back into the camp. This is to be a permanent rule for you. On the tenth day of the seventh month you are to humble yourselves by fasting and do no work of any kind. This applies to the native-born and to the outsider who lives among you. For on this day atonement will be made for you to cleanse you, so that before the LORD you are clean of all your sins. It is a Sabbath of complete rest for you, a day to humble yourselves by fasting. This is a permanent rule. The atonement is to be made by the priest who has been anointed and ordained to serve as priest in his father’s place. He is to put on the linen garments, the holy garments, and make atonement for the holy sanctuary, for the tent of meeting and for the altar, and also for the priests and for all the people of the assembly. This is to be a permanent rule for you, that once a year atonement is made for the Israelites for all their sins.” And Aaron did as the LORD had commanded Moses.

fields.title: Leviticus 17
fields.body_html:
Where sacrifices are to be offered

The LORD spoke to Moses. He said, “Speak to Aaron and his sons and to all the Israelites, and tell them: This is what the LORD has commanded: Anyone from the people of Israel who slaughters an ox, a sheep or a goat, whether in the camp or outside it, and does not bring it to the entrance of the tent of meeting to present it as an offering to the LORD in front of the tabernacle of the LORD, is to be held guilty of bloodshed. That person has shed blood and must be cut off from among the people, so that the Israelites will bring to the LORD the sacrifices they have been making out in the open country. They are to bring them to the priest at the entrance of the tent of meeting and sacrifice them to the LORD as peace offerings. The priest is to splash the blood on the altar of the LORD at the entrance of the tent of meeting and burn the fat as a soothing aroma to the LORD. They must no longer offer their sacrifices to the goat-demons that they have been chasing after like a prostitute. This is to be a permanent rule for them for all their generations. Tell them also: Anyone from the people of Israel, or from the outsiders who live among them, who offers a burnt offering or a sacrifice and does not bring it to the entrance of the tent of meeting to offer it to the LORD, must be cut off from the people. If anyone from the people of Israel or from the outsiders who live among them eats any blood, I will set my face against that person who eats the blood and will cut that person off from among the people. The life of every creature is in its blood. I have given the blood to you to make atonement on the altar for your lives, because the blood makes atonement by means of the life that is in it. That is why I have said to the Israelites, ‘None of you may eat blood, and neither may any outsider who lives among you.’

Draining the blood of game

When anyone from the Israelites or from the outsiders who live among them hunts down a wild animal or a bird that may be eaten, they must drain out its blood and cover it with earth. For the life of every creature is its blood; its blood is its life. That is why I have said to the Israelites, ‘You must not eat the blood of any creature.’ For the life of every creature is its blood, and anyone who eats it must be cut off. Anyone, whether native-born or outsider, who eats an animal that has died or one torn by wild beasts must wash their clothes and bathe in water and will be unclean until evening; then they will be clean. But if they do not wash their clothes or bathe their body, they will bear the consequences of their guilt.”

fields.title: Leviticus 18
fields.body_html:
Do not live like Egypt or Canaan

The LORD spoke to Moses. He said, “Speak to the Israelites and tell them: ‘I am the LORD your God. Do not copy what is done in the land of Egypt, where you once lived, or what is done in the land of Canaan, where I am bringing you. Do not live by their customs. You are to carry out my rulings and keep my statutes, living by them. I am the LORD your God. Keep my statutes and my rulings. The one who does them will live by them. I am the LORD.

Forbidden sexual relations

Not one of you is to go near any close relative of his own flesh to have sexual relations. I am the LORD.

You must not have sexual relations with your mother, for that would be an offense against your father. She is your mother. Do not have sexual relations with her.

Do not have sexual relations with your father’s wife. That would be an offense against your father.

You must not have sexual relations with a sister of yours, the daughter of your father or of your mother, whether she was born into your household or born outside it.

You must not have sexual relations with your son’s daughter or your daughter’s daughter, for they are your own flesh and blood.

Your father’s wife may have borne him a daughter; she is your sister, and you must not have sexual relations with her.

You must not have sexual relations with your father’s sister. She is your father’s blood relative.

You must not have sexual relations with your mother’s sister, for she is your mother’s blood relative.

Do not go near the wife of your father’s brother to have sexual relations with her, for that would be an offense against your uncle. She is your aunt.

You must not have sexual relations with your daughter-in-law. She is married to your son. Do not have sexual relations with her.

You must not have sexual relations with the wife of your brother. It would be an offense against him.

You must not have sexual relations with a woman and also with her daughter. Nor are you to marry her son’s daughter or her daughter’s daughter and have sexual relations with her. They are blood relatives; it is depravity. While your wife is alive, you must not also marry her sister, making the two women rivals by having sexual relations with her as well. While a woman is unclean because of her monthly period, you must not go near her for sexual relations. You must not have intercourse with the wife of a fellow Israelite. It would make you unclean through her. None of your children may be handed over and made to pass through the fire to Molech. You must not profane the name of your God. I am the LORD. You must not lie with a male as a man lies with a woman. It is a detestable act. You must not have intercourse with any animal; it would make you unclean. No woman is to offer herself to an animal so that it mates with her. That is a perverse mixing. Do not let any of these things make you unclean. All of them are what made the nations unclean, the nations I am driving out from before you. The land was made unclean, and I called it to account for its guilt; and the land vomited out the people living on it. But you are to keep my statutes and my rulings and not do any of these detestable things, neither the native-born nor the outsider who lives among you, for the people who lived in the land before you did all these detestable things, and the land became unclean. Then the land will not vomit you out for making it unclean, as it vomited out the nation that was there before you. For if anyone does any of these detestable things, the persons who do them must be cut off from the people. Keep what I have charged you to do. Do not take up any of the detestable customs of those who lived here before you, and do not make yourselves unclean through them. I am the LORD your God.’”

fields.title: Leviticus 19
fields.body_html:
Be holy, because I am holy

The LORD spoke to Moses. He said, “Speak to the whole congregation of the Israelites and tell them: ‘You must be holy, because I, the LORD your God, am holy. Every one of you is to show reverence to mother and father, and you are to keep my Sabbaths. I am the LORD your God. Do not turn aside to idols, and do not make yourselves gods of molten metal. I am the LORD your God. When you sacrifice a peace offering to the LORD, sacrifice it in the way that wins acceptance for you. Eat it on the day of your sacrifice or on the following day, and burn with fire whatever is still left on the third day. If any of it is eaten on the third day, it has become foul meat and will not be accepted. Anyone who eats it will bear the consequences of their guilt, because they have profaned what is holy to the LORD. That person must be cut off from the people. When you gather in your land’s harvest, do not cut the grain right up to the edges of your field, and do not collect what is left lying after the reapers. Do not go back through your vineyard to take every last cluster, or collect the grapes that drop to the ground. Leave them for the poor and for the outsider. I am the LORD your God. Do not steal, do not deny what you owe, and do not deal dishonestly with one another. Do not take an oath in my name to back up a lie; that would profane the name of your God. I am the LORD. Do not exploit your neighbor or take what is theirs by force. When you hire a laborer, the pay must not stay in your hands overnight until morning. Do not curse someone who is deaf, and do not set something in the path of someone who is blind to make them trip. Fear your God. I am the LORD. Do not do wrong when you judge a case. Do not take the side of the poor because they are poor, and do not give special honor to the powerful. Judge your fellow citizen fairly. Do not go from one person to another spreading slander among your people. Do not take a stand against your neighbor’s life. I am the LORD. Do not hold hatred in your heart for one of your own people. Be sure to correct your neighbor when they do wrong, so that you do not carry sin because of them. Do not pay back any of your own people with revenge, and do not keep holding a grudge against them. Instead, love your neighbor as yourself. I am the LORD. Keep my statutes. Do not let two different kinds of your animals breed together. Do not sow your field with two kinds of seed. Do not put on clothing made from two kinds of thread mixed together.

A slave woman promised to another man

If a man has sexual relations with a woman who is a slave promised to another man, and she has not been bought back or given her freedom, compensation must be paid. They are not to be put to death, since she was not free. The man is to bring a ram to the entrance of the tent of meeting as his guilt offering to the LORD. With the ram of the guilt offering the priest is to make atonement for him before the LORD for the sin he committed, and he will be forgiven for that sin.

Fruit trees, mourning and other laws

When you enter the land and plant any tree that bears food, you are to regard its fruit as uncircumcised. For three years it will be uncircumcised for you, and none of it may be eaten. In the fourth year all its fruit is to be set apart as holy, given in praise to the LORD. From the fifth year on you may eat its fruit. Doing this will make the tree yield more for you. I am the LORD your God. Do not eat anything with its blood still in it. Do not try to read the future, whether by divining or by soothsaying. Do not shave off the hair around the sides of your head, and do not cut away the corners of your beard. Do not gash your flesh in mourning for the dead, and do not mark your skin with tattoos. I am the LORD. Do not dishonor your daughter by giving her over to prostitution, or the land will prostitute itself and fill up with lewd wickedness. You are to keep my Sabbaths and stand in awe of my sanctuary. I am the LORD. Do not consult mediums or spiritists. Do not seek their help, or you will become unclean through them. I am the LORD your God. Rise to your feet in the presence of the gray-haired, and give honor to the old. Fear your God. I am the LORD.

Love the outsider and keep honest measures

If an outsider comes to live among you in your land, you are not to take advantage of them. The outsider living among you is to count as one of your own native-born. You are to love them as yourself, since you yourselves were outsiders in the land of Egypt. I am the LORD your God. Do not act unjustly when you decide cases, or when you measure length, weight or volume. Keep scales that are true and weights that are true, and a true dry measure (about 20 quarts) and a true liquid measure (about a gallon). I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt. Keep all my statutes and all my rulings, and put them into practice. I am the LORD.’”

fields.title: Leviticus 20
fields.body_html:
Penalties for sin

The LORD spoke to Moses. He said, “Tell the Israelites: ‘Anyone from the Israelites, or from the outsiders living in Israel, who gives any of their children to Molech, to be made to pass through the fire, must be put to death. The people of the land are to stone that person. I myself will set my face against that person and will cut them off from among the people. For by giving a child to Molech, that person has made my sanctuary unclean and profaned my holy name. If the people of the land look the other way when that person gives one of their children to Molech, and do not put that person to death, then I will set my face against that person and their family, and I will cut off from among the people both that person and all who follow them in prostituting themselves to Molech. If anyone turns to mediums and spiritists, and so prostitutes themselves by following them, I will set my face against that person and cut them off from among the people. Keep yourselves consecrated, and be holy, because I am the LORD your God. Keep my statutes and follow them. I am the LORD; I make you holy. Anyone who curses father or mother must be put to death. Since they have cursed father or mother, the guilt for their death is their own. When a man commits adultery with a married woman, the wife of a fellow Israelite, the man and the woman who have committed adultery must both be put to death. If a man has sexual relations with his father’s wife, he has committed an offense against his father. Both of them must be put to death; the guilt for their deaths is their own. If a man has sexual relations with his daughter-in-law, both of them must be put to death. They have done a perverse mixing; the guilt for their deaths is their own. If a man lies with a male as a man lies with a woman, the two of them have done a detestable act. They must be put to death; the guilt for their deaths is their own. A man who marries a woman and her mother as well has committed depravity. He and the two women are to be burned with fire. Then such depravity will not remain among you. A man who has intercourse with an animal must be put to death, and you are to kill the animal as well. When a woman goes to an animal to mate with it, you must kill the woman and the animal. Both must be put to death; the guilt for their deaths is their own. If a man marries his sister, his father’s daughter or his mother’s daughter, and they have sexual relations, it is a disgrace. They must be cut off in the sight of their people. He has had sexual relations with his sister, and he will bear the consequences of his guilt. If a man lies with a woman during her monthly period and has sexual relations with her, he has bared the place her blood flows from, and she has let it be uncovered. Both of them must be cut off from the people. Do not have sexual relations with your mother’s sister or your father’s sister, for that is to lay bare a close relative. They will bear the consequences of their guilt. If a man has sexual relations with his uncle’s wife, he has committed an offense against his uncle. They will bear the consequences of their sin and die without children. A man who marries his brother’s wife does an unclean thing. He has committed an offense against his brother; the two of them will be childless. Keep all my statutes and all my rulings, and carry them out. Then the land to which I am bringing you to make your home will not vomit you out. Do not follow the practices of the nation I am driving out ahead of you. They did all these things, and I came to loathe them. I have told you that you will take over their land; I myself will give it to you to possess, a land flowing with milk and honey. I am the LORD your God; I have set you apart from the other peoples. So you must distinguish between clean and unclean animals and between unclean and clean birds. Do not make yourselves detestable through any animal or bird or anything that creeps on the ground, the creatures I have marked off for you as unclean. You must be holy to me, because I, the LORD, am holy. I have set you apart from the other peoples so that you will belong to me. A man or a woman who is a medium or a spiritist must be put to death. They are to be stoned; the guilt for their deaths is their own.’”

fields.title: Leviticus 21
fields.body_html:
The holiness of priests

The LORD said to Moses, “Speak to the priests, Aaron’s sons, and tell them: ‘No priest is to make himself unclean for a dead person among his people, unless it is one of his nearest relatives: his mother, his father, his son, his daughter, his brother, or his sister who has never married and so, having no husband, remains close to him. For her he may become unclean. But as a husband among his people he is not to make himself unclean for his wife’s kin; that would profane him. Priests are not to make bald patches on their heads, shave the edges of their beards, or gash their bodies. They are to be holy to their God and are not to profane the name of their God. It is they who present the LORD’s food offerings, the food of their God, so they are to be holy. They must not marry a woman who has been a prostitute or who has been defiled, nor a woman divorced from her husband, because each priest is holy to his God. You must treat him as holy, because he presents the food of your God. He is to be holy to you, because I, the LORD, who make you holy, am holy. A priest’s daughter who profanes herself through prostitution profanes her father. She is to be burned with fire.

The priest who ranks above his brothers

The priest who ranks above his brothers has had the anointing oil poured on his head and has been ordained to wear the sacred garments. He must never let his hair hang loose or tear his clothes in grief. He is not to go near any dead body, not even his father’s or his mother’s, and so make himself unclean. He must not leave the sanctuary or profane the sanctuary of his God, because he bears the consecration of his God’s anointing oil. I am the LORD. He is to take as his wife a woman who is a virgin. A widow, a divorced woman, a woman profaned by prostitution: none of these may he marry. His wife must be a virgin from his own people. Otherwise he would profane his children among his people. I am the LORD; I make him holy.’”

Priests with a physical defect

The LORD spoke to Moses. He said, “Tell Aaron: ‘If any of your descendants, in any generation, has a physical defect, he is not to approach to present the food of his God. Any man with a defect is barred from coming near: a blind man or a lame one, a man with a disfigured nose or with a limb too long, a man with an injured foot or an injured hand, a hunchback or a dwarf, a man with something wrong in his eye, with a festering rash or scabs, or with crushed testicles. Whoever among the descendants of Aaron the priest has a defect is not to approach to present the LORD’s food offerings. Because of his defect he is not to approach to present the food of his God. He may eat the food of his God, both the most holy offerings and the holy offerings. Yet he is not to go in as far as the curtain or approach the altar, since he has a defect. He must not profane my holy places, for I am the LORD, who makes them holy.’” Moses passed on these words to Aaron, to his sons and to all the Israelites.

fields.title: Leviticus 22
fields.body_html:
Who may eat the holy food

The LORD spoke to Moses. He said, “Tell Aaron and his sons to be careful with the holy gifts that the Israelites set apart for me, and so not profane my holy name. I am the LORD. Say to them: ‘For all your generations, if any man among your descendants comes near the holy gifts that the Israelites consecrate to the LORD while he is unclean, that person must be cut off from before me. I am the LORD.’ No man descended from Aaron who has a serious skin disease or a discharge may eat any of the holy food until he is clean. Nor may one who touches anything made unclean by a dead body, or a man who has an emission of semen, or one who touches any swarming creature that makes him unclean, or a human being through whom he becomes unclean in any of the ways a person can be unclean, the one who has touched it stays unclean until evening and may not eat any of the holy food until he has washed his body in water. Once the sun has set he is clean, and then he may eat of the holy food, since that is what he lives on. He must not eat an animal that has died or one torn by wild beasts, and so become unclean by it. I am the LORD. The priests must guard what I have entrusted to them, or they will bear sin because of the holy food and die for having profaned it. I am the LORD, who makes them holy. No layperson may eat holy food. Neither a resident staying with a priest nor a worker he hires may eat it. But a person whom a priest has bought with his money may eat of it, and so may the slaves born in his house. They may share his food. A priest’s daughter who is married to a layman may not eat from the holy portions set aside as contributions. But a priest’s daughter who has lost her husband through death or divorce, who has no children, and who has returned to her father’s house as when she was a girl, may again share her father’s food. Still, no layperson may eat it.

If anyone eats holy food unintentionally, that person is to repay the priest for the holy food, adding a fifth to it. The priests must not profane the holy gifts that the Israelites set aside for the LORD, for if they let the people eat their holy gifts, they would load them with guilt that calls for a guilt offering. I am the LORD, who makes them holy.”

Offerings must be without defect

The LORD spoke to Moses. He said, “Speak to Aaron and his sons and to all the Israelites, and tell them: ‘Anyone from the people of Israel or from the outsiders living in Israel who presents an offering to the LORD as a burnt offering, whether for a vow they have made or as a freewill offering, then, to be accepted for you, it must be a male without defect from the cattle, the sheep or the goats. Whatever has a defect you must not offer; it will not win acceptance for you. If anyone brings the LORD a peace offering from the herd or the flock, whether to pay a vow or as a freewill offering, the animal must be without defect if it is to be accepted. There must be nothing at all wrong with it. You must not present to the LORD an animal that is blind, has a broken limb or is maimed, or one with a running sore, a festering rash or scabs. Do not give any of them to the LORD as a food offering on the altar. If an ox or a sheep has a limb too long or stunted, you may still give it as a freewill offering. For a vow, though, it will not be accepted. Do not bring the LORD an animal whose testicles have been squeezed, crushed, torn or cut off. Do not do so in your land. Do not take any of these animals from a foreigner either, and present them as the food of your God. They are damaged; they have a defect and will not be accepted for you.’”

More rules for offerings

The LORD spoke to Moses. He said, “A newborn calf, lamb or kid is to be left with its mother for seven days. From the eighth day on, it will be accepted as an offering, a food offering to the LORD. Whether from the herd or the flock, a mother animal and its young must not both be slaughtered in a single day. When you sacrifice a thanksgiving offering to the LORD, do it in the way that will gain acceptance for you. Eat it on the day it is offered, and keep none of it until the next morning. I am the LORD. You are to keep my commandments and carry them out. I am the LORD. Never profane my holy name; among the Israelites I must be treated as holy. I am the LORD, who makes you holy, who brought you out of the land of Egypt to be your God. I am the LORD.”

fields.title: Leviticus 23
fields.body_html:
The Sabbath

The LORD spoke to Moses. He said, “Speak to the Israelites and tell them: ‘You are to announce the appointed festivals of the LORD as holy assemblies. These are my appointed festivals: Work may be done for six days, but the seventh day is a Sabbath of complete rest, a holy assembly. Do no work of any kind. In all your homes it is to be kept as a Sabbath for the LORD.

Passover and the Festival of Unleavened Bread

Here are the LORD’s appointed festivals, holy assemblies that you must announce when the time for each one comes. In the first month, on its fourteenth day, as evening comes on, the Passover is kept for the LORD. The fifteenth day of this month is the Festival of Unleavened Bread, held for the LORD. Eat bread made without yeast for seven days. The first day is to be a holy assembly for you, when you do none of your ordinary work. Each of the seven days, bring the LORD a food offering. On the seventh day there is again a holy assembly, with no ordinary work.’”

The sheaf of firstfruits

The LORD spoke to Moses. He said, “Speak to the Israelites and tell them: ‘When you have entered the land I am giving you and are reaping its harvest, bring the priest a sheaf from the first of your crop. On the day after the Sabbath the priest is to lift up the sheaf and wave it before the LORD, so that you will be accepted. On the day the sheaf is waved, offer a year-old male lamb without defect as a burnt offering to the LORD. Its grain offering is to be about 4 quarts of fine flour mixed with oil, a food offering to the LORD, a soothing aroma. Its drink offering is to be about a quart of wine. Until the day you bring this offering to your God, eat nothing from the new crop: no bread, no roasted grain, no fresh heads of grain. This is a permanent rule for all your generations, wherever you live.

Seven weeks to the fiftieth day

Then begin counting on the day after the Sabbath, when you brought the sheaf as a wave offering. Count seven whole weeks. The day after the seventh Sabbath will be the fiftieth day. On it bring the LORD a grain offering from the new crop. Bring two loaves from your homes to be waved as firstfruits for the LORD. Bake them with yeast, using about 4 quarts of fine flour for each. With the bread, bring seven year-old male lambs without defect, a young bull from the herd, and two rams, all as a burnt offering to the LORD. Their grain and drink offerings go with them. It is a food offering and a soothing aroma for the LORD. Offer also one male goat for a sin offering and two year-old male lambs for a peace offering. The priest is to take the bread of the firstfruits and the two lambs and wave them before the LORD as a wave offering. They are holy to the LORD, and they are for the priest. Announce a holy assembly on that very day, a day when none of your ordinary work is done. It is a permanent rule, wherever you live, for all your generations. At harvest time, leave the edges of your field uncut, and do not go back for the grain the harvesters leave behind. These are for the poor and the outsider. I am the LORD your God.’”

The day of loud blasts

The LORD spoke to Moses. He said, “Speak to the Israelites and tell them: ‘In the seventh month, the first day of the month is for you a day of Sabbath rest. Loud blasts are to be sounded as a reminder, and there is to be a holy assembly. None of your ordinary work is to be done that day, and you are to bring the LORD a food offering.’”

The Day of Atonement

The LORD spoke to Moses. He said, “Mark the tenth day of this seventh month: it is the Day of Atonement. On it you are to hold a holy assembly, humble yourselves by fasting, and bring the LORD a food offering. On that very day no work of any kind is to be done. It is a day of atonement, set for making atonement for you in the presence of the LORD your God. If anyone does not humble themselves by fasting on that day, that person must be cut off from the people. Anyone who does any work on that day I will wipe out from among the people. You must not work at all. It is a permanent rule for all your generations, wherever you live. For you it is a Sabbath of complete rest, and you must humble yourselves by fasting. Keep this Sabbath from evening to evening, beginning on the evening of the ninth day of the month.”

The Festival of Booths

The LORD spoke to Moses. He said, “Speak to the Israelites and tell them: ‘The fifteenth day of this seventh month begins the Festival of Booths, kept for the LORD seven days. The first day is a holy assembly; none of your ordinary work is to be done. Each of the seven days you are to bring the LORD a food offering. The eighth day is also a holy assembly for you, with a food offering for the LORD. It is a solemn assembly that closes the festival, and none of your ordinary work is to be done. These, then, are the LORD’s appointed festivals. Announce them as holy assemblies, at which food offerings are brought to the LORD: burnt offerings and grain offerings, sacrifices and drink offerings, what each day requires on that day, over and above the LORD’s Sabbaths and over and above your gifts, all your vows and all your freewill offerings that you give to the LORD. But when you have brought in what the land has produced, keep the LORD’s festival for seven days, starting on the fifteenth day of the seventh month. On both the first day and the eighth there is to be a day of Sabbath rest. On the first day gather the fruit of fine trees, fronds from palm trees, branches from trees thick with leaves, and willows that grow by the streams. Then celebrate before the LORD your God for seven days. Each year you are to keep this seven-day festival for the LORD. It is a permanent rule for all your generations that you keep it in the seventh month. For seven days you are to stay in booths. Everyone born an Israelite must live in booths, so that every generation of yours may know this: when I brought the Israelites out of the land of Egypt, I made them live in booths. I am the LORD your God.’” In this way Moses made known the appointed festivals of the LORD to the Israelites.

fields.title: Leviticus 24
fields.body_html:
The lamps in the tent of meeting

The LORD spoke to Moses. He said, “Command the Israelites to bring you pure oil from crushed olives to give light, so that a lamp may burn there without fail. Aaron is to set it in order in the tent of meeting, outside the curtain in front of the testimony, so that it burns before the LORD from evening until morning without fail. This is a permanent rule for all your generations. He is to set the lamps in order on the pure gold lampstand before the LORD, without fail.

The twelve loaves

You are to take fine flour and bake it into twelve loaves. Each loaf is to contain about 4 quarts. Set them out on the pure gold table before the LORD, in two rows with six loaves to a row. Put pure frankincense on each row. It is to be a memorial portion for the bread, a food offering to the LORD. Every Sabbath day he is to set it out before the LORD, without fail. It comes from the Israelites as a covenant that lasts forever. The bread is to go to Aaron and his sons, and they must eat it in a holy place, because it is most holy for him, his permanent share of the food offerings to the LORD.”

A man who blasphemed the Name

A man whose mother was an Israelite and whose father was an Egyptian went out among the Israelites. In the camp he got into a fight with an Israelite man. The Israelite woman’s son blasphemed the Name, uttering curses, and they brought him to Moses. His mother’s name was Shelomith, Dibri’s daughter, of the tribe of Dan. They held him under guard, waiting for a clear ruling from the LORD.

Life for life

The LORD spoke to Moses. He said, “Take the one who cursed outside the camp. Everyone who heard him must lay their hands on his head, and then the whole congregation is to stone him. Say to the Israelites: ‘If anyone curses their God, they will bear the consequences of their sin. Whoever blasphemes the name of the LORD must be put to death. The whole congregation must stone that person. The outsider is no different from the native-born: whoever blasphemes the Name must die. Anyone who strikes and kills another human being must be put to death. Whoever kills an animal belonging to someone else must replace it: life for life. If anyone injures a neighbor, what they did is to be done to them. a broken bone for a broken bone, an eye for an eye, a tooth for a tooth. The same injury they caused to someone else is to be caused to them. To kill an animal means paying for it; to kill a person means being put to death. There is to be a single standard of justice for you, the same for outsider and native-born alike, for I am the LORD your God.’” Moses passed this on to the Israelites, and they brought the man who had cursed out of the camp and killed him with stones. The Israelites did exactly what the LORD had commanded Moses.

fields.title: Leviticus 25
fields.body_html:
The Sabbath year

The LORD spoke to Moses on Mount Sinai. He said, “Speak to the Israelites and tell them: ‘When you enter the land I am giving you, the land is to have a Sabbath rest in honor of the LORD. For six years you may plant your fields and trim your vineyards and gather what they yield. But the seventh year is to be a Sabbath of complete rest for the land, a Sabbath for the LORD, when you neither sow your fields nor prune your vineyards. Do not harvest the grain that comes up on its own from the last crop, and do not pick the grapes from the vines you have left unpruned. It is to be a year of complete rest for the land. Whatever the land produces in its Sabbath year will be food for all of you: for you, your male and female servants, your hired worker, and the resident who stays with you, and for your livestock and for the wild animals in your land. All that the land yields may be eaten.

The year of Jubilee

Count off seven Sabbaths of years, seven times seven years. The time of the seven Sabbaths of years will come to forty-nine years. Then on the tenth day of the seventh month send the loud blast of the ram’s horn out across the country. On the Day of Atonement have the horn sounded through all your land. Set the fiftieth year apart as holy, and announce freedom in the land for everyone who lives in it. This will be your Jubilee, when each of you goes home to your own property and to your own clan. That fiftieth year is to be your Jubilee. Do not sow, and do not harvest what springs up by itself or pick the grapes from the unpruned vines. For it is a Jubilee, and it is to be holy to you. Eat what the field gives, straight from the field. This Jubilee year is when each of you goes home to your own property. When you sell land to your neighbor or buy it from your neighbor, do not cheat one another. The price you pay your neighbor is to depend on how many years have gone by since the Jubilee, and the price he asks is to depend on how many years of harvests remain. If many years are left, the price goes up; if only a few, it goes down. For he is selling you a certain number of harvests. So do not cheat one another; fear your God instead. I am the LORD your God. Put my statutes into practice, and be careful to keep my rules. Then you will live in safety on the land. The land will produce its fruit, you will have all you want to eat, and you will be safe living there. You might ask, “What are we to eat in the seventh year, if we are not to sow or bring in our harvest?” I will order my blessing on you in the sixth year, so that the harvest of that year will be enough to last three years. When you sow in the eighth year you will still be eating from the old harvest. You will go on eating the old store until the ninth year, when that year’s crop comes in. No land is to be sold for good, for the land belongs to me. You are only outsiders and residents living with me. Throughout the land you hold, you must allow land that has been sold to be bought back.

Buying back land and houses

Suppose a fellow Israelite falls into poverty and has to sell some of his land. Then the relative closest to him, his redeemer, is to come and buy back what his kinsman sold. If someone has no one to redeem it but later prospers and gathers enough to buy it back himself, he is to work out the years since he sold it, pay the buyer back for the years that remain, and go back to his land. But if he cannot raise enough to pay him back, the land he sold stays with the buyer until the Jubilee year. In the Jubilee it is released, and he goes back to his land. If someone sells a home inside a walled city, the right to buy it back lasts until a full year has passed since he sold it. He has a year in which to redeem it. If it is not bought back before the full year is over, the house in the walled city becomes the permanent property of the buyer and his descendants. It is not released in the Jubilee. But a house in a village with no wall around it counts as part of the farmland. The right to buy it back remains, and at the Jubilee it goes back to its owner. In the case of the Levites’ towns, the houses in the towns they own, the Levites have the right to buy them back at any time. And if a house in one of their towns is acquired from a Levite, the sale ends at the Jubilee, for the houses in the Levites’ towns are their property among the Israelites. The pastureland around their towns may not be sold at all; it is theirs for all time.

Caring for the poor

If a fellow Israelite near you falls into poverty and can no longer provide for himself, you are to support him, and he is to live beside you like an outsider or a resident. Do not take interest from him or add anything to what he owes. Fear your God, and let your fellow Israelite keep on living with you. When you lend him money, take no interest, and when you supply him with food, take no extra back. I am the LORD your God. It was I who brought you out of the land of Egypt, so that I could give you the land of Canaan and be your God.

Israelites who sell themselves

Suppose a fellow Israelite living near you becomes so poor that he sells himself to you. You must not make him do a slave’s work. He is to stay with you on the footing of a hired worker or a resident, and work for you up to the Jubilee year. Then he and his children are to leave you and go back to his clan, and he will return to the land his ancestors held. For they are my slaves, since I brought them out of the land of Egypt. They must not be sold the way slaves are sold. Do not lord it over him with cruelty. Fear your God. If you want male or female slaves, you may buy them from the nations that live around you. You may also buy them from the residents who are staying among you, and from their families who are with you and were born in your land. They may be counted among your holdings. You may hand them down to your children after you as property they will hold, and they may work for you permanently. But over your own kin, the Israelites, you must not rule harshly, one over another.

Buying back an Israelite sold to an outsider

If an outsider or resident living among you becomes rich, and a fellow Israelite near him grows poor and sells himself to that outsider or to a member of the outsider’s clan, he still has the right to be bought back after selling himself. One of his brothers may redeem him, an uncle could do it, or a cousin, or any other close relative in his clan. Or if he gets the means, he can buy himself back. Together with the man who bought him, he is to work out how many years run from the year of the sale to the Jubilee year. The money for his sale is then reckoned by those years, as though his time with the buyer were the time of a hired worker. If there are still many years to go, he is to give back a matching part of the money paid for him to buy his freedom. If only a few years remain before the Jubilee year, he is to reckon them up and pay for his freedom in line with those years. He is to live with the buyer like a worker hired from year to year, and you must not let the buyer treat him harshly while you look on. Even if no one redeems him by these means, he and his children are to go free in the Jubilee year. For the Israelites are slaves who belong to me. They are my slaves, the people I brought out of the land of Egypt. I am the LORD your God.

fields.title: Leviticus 26
fields.body_html:
No idols

Do not make worthless idols for yourselves, and do not set up a carved image or a sacred pillar. Do not place a stone carved with images anywhere in your land in order to bow down before it, for I am the LORD your God. You are to keep my Sabbaths and stand in awe of my sanctuary. I am the LORD.

Blessings for obedience

If you live by my statutes and faithfully keep my commandments, then I will send you rain at the right season; the land will yield its crops, and the trees of the field their fruit. Threshing will keep you busy until the grape harvest, and the grape harvest until it is time to sow. You will have bread enough to be satisfied, and you will live in your land secure. I will give peace in the land, and you will lie down to sleep with no one to frighten you. I will rid the land of harmful beasts, and no sword will cross your land. You will chase your enemies, and they will fall by the sword in front of you. Five of you will put 100 to flight, and 100 of you will rout 10,000. Your enemies will fall before you by the sword. I will turn toward you with favor, make you fruitful and increase your numbers, and I will uphold my covenant with you. You will still be eating from last year’s harvest, long stored, when you have to clear it out to make room for the new. I will set my dwelling place in your midst, and I will not turn from you in loathing. I will go about among you. I will be God to you, and you will be my people. I am the LORD your God. I brought you out of the land of Egypt, where you were their slaves. I snapped the crossbars of the yoke on your neck and made you walk upright.

Punishment for disobedience

But if you will not listen to me and do not carry out all these commandments, if you reject my statutes and loathe my rulings, so that you fail to keep all my commandments and so break my covenant, then I too will do this to you: I will send panic upon you, with wasting disease and burning fever that wear out the eyes and wear down the spirit. You will sow your seed and gain nothing from it, for your enemies will eat the harvest. I will turn my face against you, and you will go down in defeat before your enemies. Your foes will rule you, and you will run when there is no one chasing you.

Seven times more for your sins

If even after these things you do not listen to me, I will go on to discipline you seven times more for your sins. I will break the strength you are proud of. I will make your sky hard as iron and your soil hard as bronze. You will wear yourselves out for nothing. Your land will not give its crops, and the trees in the land will not give their fruit. If you keep walking in opposition to me and refuse to listen to me, I will strike you with blows seven times more, as your sins deserve. I will send the wild animals among you. They will take your children from you, wipe out your herds, and leave you so few that no one travels your roads. If you will not accept my discipline even through these things, and you keep walking in opposition to me, then I too will walk in opposition to you, and it is I who will strike you seven times over for your sins. I will bring a sword against you that will carry out the vengeance of the covenant. When you crowd into your cities for safety, I will send deadly disease among you, and you will be handed over to your enemy. When I break the staff that is your bread, there will be so little that ten women can bake it all in a single oven. They will hand it back to you weighed out, and you will eat and still be hungry.

Exile, and the covenant remembered

If in spite of this you still will not listen to me, but keep walking in opposition to me, then I will walk in furious opposition to you, and I too will discipline you seven times over for your sins. You will eat the flesh of your sons, and you will eat the flesh of your daughters. I will destroy your hilltop shrines and cut down your incense altars. I will throw your dead bodies on the carcasses of your idols, and I will loathe you. I will turn your cities into ruins and make your sanctuaries desolate. I will not smell the soothing aroma you offer. It is I who will lay the land waste, so that your enemies who settle in it will be appalled. As for you, I will scatter you among the nations and draw a sword to chase after you. Your land will be left desolate and your cities in ruins. So the land will at last enjoy its Sabbaths through all the time it lies desolate, while you are in your enemies’ land. Then the land will rest and enjoy its Sabbaths. Through all its days of desolation it will rest, as it never rested in your Sabbaths while you were living there. On those of you who survive I will bring despair of heart in the lands of their enemies. The rustle of a leaf in the wind will chase them, and they will run as people run from a sword, and fall with no one behind them. They will tumble over one another as though a sword were behind them, when there is no pursuer at all. You will have no strength to make a stand against your enemies. Among the nations you will perish; your enemies’ land will eat you up. And the survivors among you will waste away under their guilt in your enemies’ lands; under their fathers’ guilt as well, which is with them, they will waste away. But if they confess their guilt and the guilt of their fathers, the unfaithfulness they committed against me, and confess too that they walked in opposition to me, so that I too walked in opposition to them and brought them into the land of their enemies; if then their uncircumcised hearts are humbled, and they accept the punishment for their guilt, then I will remember my covenant with Jacob, and my covenant with Isaac, and my covenant with Abraham I will remember as well; and I will remember the land. For the land will be left behind by them and will enjoy its Sabbaths while it lies desolate without them, and they will accept the punishment for their guilt, for the very reason that they rejected my rulings and loathed my statutes. But even then, while they are in their enemies’ land, I will not cast them off, nor will I loathe them so much that I make an end of them and break my covenant with them. For I am the LORD their God. I will remember, for their good, the covenant I made with the generation before them, whom I led out of the land of Egypt while the nations looked on, to be their God. I am the LORD.’” These are the statutes, the rulings and the instructions that the LORD set between himself and the Israelites on Mount Sinai through Moses.

fields.title: Leviticus 27
fields.body_html:
Vows of people

The LORD spoke to Moses. He said, “Speak to the Israelites and tell them: ‘When anyone makes a special vow to give the LORD the value of a person, the valuation for a man from twenty to sixty years of age is to be fifty shekels of silver, measured by the sanctuary shekel. If it is a woman, the valuation is thirty shekels. For someone from five to twenty years of age, the valuation is twenty shekels for a male and ten shekels for a female. For a child from one month to five years old, the valuation is five shekels of silver for a male and three shekels of silver for a female. For someone sixty years old or more, the valuation is fifteen shekels for a man and ten shekels for a woman. But if the one who vows is too poor to pay the valuation, the person is to be brought before the priest, and the priest will set a value for them, fixing the amount by what the one who vowed is able to pay.

Vows of animals, houses and fields

If the vow is of an animal of the kind that may be presented as an offering to the LORD, any such animal given to the LORD becomes holy. The owner must not swap it or put another in its place, a good animal for a poor one or a poor one for a good one. If they do replace one animal with another, both the first animal and the one put in its place will be holy. If the vow is of an unclean animal, of the kind that may not be presented as an offering to the LORD, the animal is to be brought before the priest, and the priest will set its value according to whether it is good or poor. The value he sets will stand. If the owner does redeem it, they must pay the valuation and a fifth more. When anyone consecrates a house as holy to the LORD, the priest is to judge whether it is in good or poor condition and set its value. The value the priest sets will stand. If the one who consecrated the house wants to redeem it, they must pay its value in silver and a fifth more, and it will be theirs again. If anyone consecrates to the LORD part of a field that is their family’s land, its value will follow the seed needed to sow it: fifty shekels of silver for about 6 bushels of barley seed. If the field is consecrated from the Year of Jubilee onward, the full valuation will stand. But if the field is consecrated after the Jubilee, the priest will work out the price by the years left until the next Year of Jubilee, and the valuation will be reduced to match. If the one who consecrated the field does redeem it, they must pay its value in silver and a fifth more, and it will remain theirs. But if they do not redeem the field, or if the field has been sold to someone else, it can never again be redeemed. When the field is released in the Jubilee, it will be holy to the LORD, like a field that is devoted to him. It will belong to the priest as his own land. If someone consecrates to the LORD a field they have bought, which is not part of their family’s land, the priest will work out the amount of the valuation up to the Year of Jubilee, and that person must pay the valuation on the same day as a holy gift to the LORD. In the Year of Jubilee the field will go back to the one from whom it was bought, the one whose family land it is. Every valuation is to be by the sanctuary shekel, which is twenty gerahs.

Firstborn, devoted things and tithes

But no one may consecrate the firstborn of an animal, since a firstborn already belongs to the LORD. Whether it is from the cattle or the flock, it is the LORD’s. If it is an unclean animal, the owner may buy it back at its valuation, adding a fifth to it. If it is not redeemed, it is to be sold at its valuation. But anything that anyone devotes to the LORD from what they own, whether human or animal or a field they hold as family land, may not be sold and may not be bought back. All that is devoted is most holy to the LORD. When a human being has been placed under the ban for destruction, no ransom may be paid for them; they must be put to death. All the tithe of the land belongs to the LORD, both grain from what is sown and fruit from the trees. It is holy to the LORD. If anyone wants to redeem any of their tithe, they must add a fifth to its value. As for the herd and the flock, of all the animals that pass under the rod as they are counted, every tenth one will be holy to the LORD. The owner is not to look over the animals to sort good from poor, and must not exchange one for another. If they do make an exchange, the animal and the one put in its place will both be holy, and neither can be redeemed.’” These are the commandments the LORD laid on Moses for the Israelites, on Mount Sinai.

fields.title: Conclusion
fields.body_html:
These are the commandments the LORD laid on Moses for the Israelites, on Mount Sinai.

— Leviticus 27:34

Leviticus ends as quietly as it began. There is no battle, no journey, no death of a hero. The last chapter is about vows and tithes, the gifts people promise to God and how they may redeem them, and then a single sentence telling us where all of this was spoken. The camp is still at Sinai. The cloud still rests on the tent. But Israel now knows how to live with the God who lives among them.

The question the book leaves with you

Leviticus asks more of its readers than any book before it. “You must be holy, because I am holy.” It reaches into kitchens and fields, into marriages and markets, into the way a worker is paid and a blind man is treated. And it is honest about how far short people fall. The priests who stand nearest to God die for their carelessness on the first day. The high priest must make atonement for his own sins before he can make it for anyone else’s. And the great Day of Atonement has to come round again every year.

So the book leaves an ache. Can anyone really come near to God? Can sin ever be taken away for good, and not only covered for another year? Can holiness be more than a rule from outside? The letter to the Hebrews puts the question plainly: “For the law holds only a shadow of the good things to come, not the very form of the things themselves.” The sacrifices “bring sins back to mind every year, because the blood of bulls and goats cannot take sins away.”

Where the book points

The New Testament answers by pointing to Jesus as everything Leviticus describes. He is the priest: “We have, then, a great high priest who has gone through the heavens: Jesus the Son of God.” He is the sacrifice, the one John the Baptist called “the Lamb of God, who carries away the sin of the world”. He is the one who touched the unclean and made them clean. And by his death the curtain that hid the Most Holy Place is opened to all his people:

“So then, brothers and sisters, the blood of Jesus has given us confidence to go into the sanctuary. He has opened for us a way that is new and living, a way through the curtain, which is his flesh.”

— Hebrews 10:19–20

Leviticus does not become useless once Christ has come. Its command to holiness is quoted by Peter: “You are to be holy, because I am holy.” Its second great commandment, love of neighbour, is the one Jesus set beside the first. And its whole language of offering is taken up by Paul, who asks the church to “offer your bodies to God as a living sacrifice, holy and pleasing to him.” The altar has moved, but the call to come near has not.

Where to go from here

Leviticus is best read with company. Some of the best in this library:

  • On the whole book. Hannah Whitall Smith’s Old Testament Types and Teachings, whose chapter “Leviticus: Communion” reads the book as a guide to fellowship with God.
  • On the priesthood and the Day of Atonement. The Letter to the Hebrews in this library’s Open Word Bible edition, the New Testament’s own commentary on Leviticus; F. B. Meyer’s The Way into the Holiest, an exposition of Hebrews, with chapters on “The True Tabernacle” and “The Blood of Christ”; and Charles H. Spurgeon’s Salvation to the Uttermost, on Christ the priest who is “always alive to plead on their behalf” (Hebrews 7:25).
  • On the veil and the Most Holy Place. Horatius Bonar’s The Rent Veil, which moves from the veil of the tabernacle to the veil torn at the cross and the blood carried within it.
  • On the bread of God (Leviticus 21:22). Horatius Bonar’s The Divine Banquet, which reads the bread of the presence, eaten by the priests, as a picture of Christ.
  • On the covenant with Levi. Andrew Murray’s The Two Covenants, with its chapter “The Covenant of an Everlasting Priesthood”, on the tribe of Levi as a picture of the priesthood every believer is called to share.
  • On atonement. William Booth’s The Atonement of Jesus Christ and William J. Seymour’s The Precious Atonement, two sermons on what the blood of Christ accomplishes.
  • On being holy (Leviticus 19:2). J. C. Ryle’s Holiness, whose title chapter, on Hebrews 12:14, asks what practical holiness looks like.

You can also go the other way, from the text to the classics. Every reference to Leviticus in this library can be tapped to read the verse, and the Scripture pages gather, chapter by chapter, what the great writers of the church have said about each passage of this book.

And then read on. In Numbers the cloud lifts, and the holy people who have learned to live around the tent must carry it through the wilderness. They go with the promise at the heart of Leviticus:

I will go about among you. I will be God to you, and you will be my people.

— Leviticus 26:12
